info.bio:
Rites of Spring fue una banda de hardcore punk formada en Washington DC, Estados Unidos en marzo de 1984 y estaba compuesta por el guitarrista/letrista y cantante Guy Picciotto, guitarrista Eddie Janney, bajista Mike Fellows, y el baterista Brendan Canty.

scenes.name: Hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk como «violento, rápido y ruidoso» tarda en conquistar EE UU, pero cuando lo hace el hardcore se convierte durante dos décadas en el idioma nacional de millones de chavales. Misfits y el «scum-rock»; el crossover punk-metal (Suicidal Tendencies, Corrosion Of Conformity, Agnostic Front); Mission Of Burma en Boston. Washington: Bad Brains (reggae, funk y metal diez años por delante), Minor Threat (el «straight-edge») y Rites Of Spring, inventores del emo-core. San Francisco: Dead Kennedys de Jello Biafra, D.R.I. (thrash antes que Metallica), Flipper. Los «beach punks» de Los Ángeles: Germs, X, Black Flag (Damaged), Descendents, Gun Club (Fire Of Love), Bad Religion. El jazz-core de Minutemen y Saccharine Trust; en el Medio Oeste, Husker Du y Replacements cambian el hardcore para siempre; en Chicago, Naked Raygun y Big Black de Steve Albini; en Europa, The Ex y los italianos CCCP.

podcast.title: D.C. Scene Origins of Emo
podcast.body: Rites of Spring emerged from the Washington D.C. scene in the mid-1980s, which is credited as a crucial birthplace for emo. The band's approach contrasted with the violence prevalent at some hardcore shows, as they chose to focus on personal lyrical themes and more melodic guitar work. "we need to give all kinds of credit to a scene in Washington, D.C. that emerged in the middle 1980s. And this is where we encounter a hardcore band called Rites of Spring."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Emo Band
podcast.body: Rites of Spring is cited as one of the early original emo bands, stemming from the Washington, D.C. hardcore punk scene and noted for its emphasis on emotional expression. "Early original emo bands included minor threat and rights of spring."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Personal Lyrical Themes
podcast.body: Diverging from common political and social themes in hardcore, Rites of Spring focused their lyrics on deeply personal subjects such as depression, bitter romanticism, and nostalgia for better times. "Rites of Spring chose to get very personal with their lyrics, depression, bitter romanticism, nostalgia for better times."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Embrace Vocalist
xref.body: Guy Picciotto, formerly the singer for Rites of Spring, also featured as a member of the proto-emo group Embrace. "Embrace also featured Rites of Spring singer Guy Piccoedo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Producer of First Emo Record
xref.body: Ian MacKaye produced Rites of Spring's self-titled 1985 record, which is widely considered by emo scholars to be the first true emo album. "Rites of Spring from 1985, produced by their Rode, a guy by the name of Ian McCleye."
